I've written the draft below. It doesn't say the change will make everyone's job better, because your own facts show that isn't true for everyone. People who have worked 9 to 5 in a branch will now face rotating shifts that can run until 8 p.m., and they'll lose face-to-face work with members. Some will see that as a step down, and those 14 people will read the email most closely. If you tell them it's better for everyone, they'll trust the rest of your message less. So the draft names the real benefits (same or higher pay, working from home, a less frantic phone queue) and is honest about what's harder.

**Fill in before sending:**
- **[bracketed items]:** the decision deadline, the center's start date, the contact person, and the meeting details.
- **Severance terms:** check with HR whether a minimum or maximum applies. Also check how partial years count, and whether a release must be signed.

**Tell the 14 staff first.** Ideally, managers or you meet with them in person before this email reaches the whole organization. Learning about a branch closing from an all-staff email lands badly.

<final_document>
**Subject: Changes to Maple Street and Route 9, and our new Member Contact Center**

Dear colleagues,

I'm writing to share a decision that affects all of us. Our Maple Street and Route 9 branches will close on March 31. We'll also open a new member phone and chat center, and everyone who works at those two branches will be offered a role there.

**Why we're doing this**

Our members are changing how they reach us. Over the last three years, visits to Maple Street and Route 9 fell 44%. Over the same period, phone and chat contacts across the credit union rose 60%. Our phone lines haven't kept up. A member who calls us today waits an average of 9 minutes on hold. That isn't the service we want to give, and it puts a lot of strain on the colleagues answering those calls.

**What this means for the 14 people at Maple Street and Route 9**

- Every one of you is offered a position in the new center at the same pay or higher.
- The center will be open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays, with rotating shifts. I know that's a real change from 9 to 5, and we'll work with you on scheduling.
- After 90 days of training, you can work from home two days a week.
- If you decide the new role isn't right for you, you'll receive two weeks of pay for every year you've worked here.

Please let your manager know your decision by [date]. Before then, you'll each have a one-on-one conversation to go through the details and answer your questions.

**What it means for everyone else**

The new center will help with call volume across all our branches and departments. Members will reach a person faster, and colleagues elsewhere should get fewer calls that come from members who have already waited too long.

**Being honest about the change**

This isn't easy news. Closing a branch means leaving a place where many of you have built relationships with members over years. For some of you, the new hours and type of work will suit you well. For others, they'll take real adjustment, and that's a fair reaction. You have my commitment that we'll treat this transition with care, and you'll have training and support from your managers throughout.

I'll be holding an open Q&A on [date/time/location or link]. You're also welcome to contact me or [HR contact] directly at any time.

Thank you for the work you do for our members every day.

[Your name]
Chief Operating Officer
</final_document>
